ai.definition: Orbital Tether Energy involves deploying a long conducting cable in orbit, which generates electricity by moving through a planet's magnetic field or transfers momentum to spacecraft.
ai.howItWorks: The tether's movement through the planet's magnetic field induces an electric current (electrodynamic effect), and its rotation can transfer angular momentum to payloads, propelling them to higher orbits without using fuel.
ai.problemSolved: Reduces the need for traditional chemical propulsion in space missions, enabling more efficient and cost-effective orbital maneuvers and power generation.
ai.manufacturing: Requires advanced materials with high tensile strength and electrical conductivity. Manufacturing involves precise engineering and deployment techniques.
ai.buildProcess: Involves designing, fabricating, and launching a conductive tether into orbit, followed by deployment and operation to generate electricity or transfer momentum.
ai.costDrivers: High initial development costs due to advanced materials and specialized launch vehicles; ongoing operational costs related to maintenance and potential failure modes.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Theoretical concept with significant research needed before practical implementation. Potential for breakthroughs but currently facing numerous technical challenges.
ai.regulation: No specific regulations exist, but any deployment would need to comply with space law and international agreements on orbital debris.
ai.risks: Technical risks include material failure, environmental factors (e.g., micrometeoroids), and operational complexities. Legal risks involve potential conflicts over orbital space.
ai.profitability: Uncertain due to current theoretical stage; could become profitable in the future with widespread adoption of tether technology for both power generation and transportation.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development likely involves overcoming material science challenges, improving deployment techniques, and demonstrating successful long-term operation in orbit.

glossary.def: The phenomenon where a conductor moving through a magnetic field induces an electric current.
Space junk resulting from past space missions, posing risks to operational satellites and future launches.

subsystems.name: Tether conductor
subsystems.role: a long conductive cable that interacts with a planet's magnetic field or carries momentum.

subsystems.name: Plasma contactor
subsystems.role: emits or collects electrons to complete the electrical circuit with the ionosphere.

subsystems.name: Deployment and tension control
subsystems.role: unreels the tether from a compact spool and keeps it taut.

subsystems.name: Power conversion and storage
subsystems.role: rectifies the induced voltage and delivers stable electricity.

subsystems.name: Payload interface
subsystems.role: for momentum-exchange use, attaches and releases a payload at the correct moment.

subsystems.name: Attitude and orbit control
subsystems.role: points the tether along the local vertical and manages orbital changes.

buildSteps.title: Design tether and orbit
buildSteps.detail: Choose a length of kilometres to tens of kilometres, conductor gauge, and an orbit that gives useful magnetic flux or momentum exchange.

buildSteps.title: Manufacture the conductor
buildSteps.detail: Braid or weave the conductor together with high-strength fibres, coat it with insulation, and test tensile strength and conductivity.

buildSteps.title: Wind and package
buildSteps.detail: Spool the tether on a reel under controlled tension and protect it against launch vibration.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the spacecraft bus
buildSteps.detail: Integrate the reel, plasma contactor, power electronics, avionics and payload interface into a small satellite or upper stage.

buildSteps.title: Launch and deploy
buildSteps.detail: Release the spacecraft, then slowly unreel the tether while using thrusters to control attitude and avoid tangling.

buildSteps.title: Establish electrical contact
buildSteps.detail: Activate the plasma contactor to close the circuit with the ionosphere, and measure current, voltage and the resulting drag or thrust.

buildSteps.title: Demonstrate energy harvest
buildSteps.detail: Convert the induced current into a stable bus voltage and feed it to a battery or payload.

buildSteps.title: Demonstrate momentum exchange
buildSteps.detail: For transport, capture a payload, spin up the tether, and release at the correct phase to reach a higher orbit.

buildSteps.title: Deorbit or retrieve
buildSteps.detail: Cut or reel in the tether at end of life to limit space debris.

prerequisites.why: fibres and conductors exist, but no tether of the required length and durability has flown reliably.
hollow cathodes have flown, but long-duration operation in the ionosphere is unproven.
satellite converters and insulation handle kilovolt levels, but need adaptation for a moving tether.
models exist, but controlling a kilometres-long flexible tether remains difficult.
docking is routine, but capturing and releasing a payload on a tether end is novel.

pathway.milestone: subscale tether flights demonstrating current generation and thrust
pathway.unlocks: data on plasma contact and tether dynamics for scaling up.

pathway.milestone: kilowatt-class electrodynamic tether for satellite deorbit
pathway.unlocks: propellant-free end-of-life disposal and limited power generation.

pathway.milestone: momentum-exchange tether transferring payloads between low Earth orbit and higher orbits
reusable tether infrastructure at a station or depot
pathway.unlocks: routine power and payload transfer, cutting launch mass for deep-space missions.
